Inverse-probability weights, or case weights for independent observations,
change the fit and the standard errors. Part of the [Models](models.html)
collection.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Structure** | any single-mediator model, fitted with weights |
| **Class returned** | `MediationData` |
| **Set with** | `weights = ` and `se_type = "sandwich"` in `fit_mediation()` |
| **Needs** | the suggested `sandwich` package for `se_type = "sandwich"` |

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Pair weights with `se_type = "sandwich"`
Model-based standard errors assume the weights are known precision weights,
which inverse-probability weights are not. medfit prints a once-per-session
message when you use `weights` with the default `se_type`.
:::

## Build stabilized weights

```{r}
#| label: weights
ps <- glm(treatment ~ covariate1 + covariate2, family = binomial(),
          data = mediation_demo)
p_t <- fitted(ps)
p_m <- mean(mediation_demo$treatment)
ipw <- ifelse(mediation_demo$treatment == 1, p_m / p_t, (1 - p_m) / (1 - p_t))
summary(ipw)
```

`mediation_demo`'s treatment is randomized, so these weights stay close to 1;
they illustrate the call, not a confounded design.

## Fit with the sandwich covariance

```{r}
#| label: fit
fit <- fit_mediation(
  outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
  mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = mediation_demo, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
  weights = ipw, se_type = "sandwich"
)
tidy(fit, type = "effects", conf.int = TRUE)
```

## What each choice does

| Choice | Effect |
|---|---|
| `weights = ipw` | both models are fitted with the weights |
| `se_type = "sandwich"` | heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC3) covariance for the estimates |
| `se_type = "model"` (default) | model-based covariance; not valid under inverse-probability weights |

## Limits

- HC3 treats the observations as independent. It does **not** handle survey
  clusters, strata or replicate weights.
- The `regmedint` engine accepts neither `weights` nor `se_type = "sandwich"`.
- The native engine takes weights too, in `fit_sem()`,
  with its own sandwich (HC0-type) covariance; see
  [Methods and Formulas](methods.html).
